papers.title_in_file: Engineering Quantum Reservoirs through Krylov Complexity, Expressivity and Observability
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study comparing Krylov-based measures with task performance in quantum reservoir computing.

assertions.value: The authors report that Krylov observability behaves almost identically to information processing capacity and is three orders of magnitude faster to compute.
quotes: Our results show that Krylov observability exhibits almost identical behavior to information processing capacity, while being three orders of times faster to compute.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulated reservoirs in one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that fidelity and spread complexity explain task performance only for short time evolutions of the quantum systems.
quotes: fidelity and spread complexity can only explain the task performance for short time evolutions of the quantum systems
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors train four distinct quantum reservoirs on a chaotic time series and larger reservoirs with random inter-spin couplings, with the Lorenz63 system as the benchmark.
quotes: We train four distinct quantum reservoirs on a chaotic time series and larger reservoirs with random inter-spin couplings.
As a benchmark the Lorenz63 system is used
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup (Introduction, p.1).

assertions.value: The authors report that when the system is undersampled, Krylov observability best captures the behavior of the task performance.
quotes: In the case when the system is undersampled Krylov observability best captures the behavior of the task performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Kernel Alignment for Quantum Support Vector Machines Using Genetic Algorithms
papers.what_it_is: A study that uses a genetic algorithm (GASP) to design QSVM kernel circuits.

assertions.value: The authors report that GASP-generated circuits match or surpass standard classical and quantum kernels in benchmarks.
quotes: Benchmarking against classical and quantum kernels reveals GASP-generated circuits matching or surpassing standard techniques.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the relationship between test accuracy and quantum kernel entropy shows little correlation.
quotes: We also analyse the relationship between test accuracy and quantum kernel entropy, with results indicating little correlation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they apply the GASP framework to gate sequence selection in QSVM kernel circuits.
quotes: we leverage the GASP (Genetic Algorithm for State Preparation) framework for gate sequence selection in QSVM kernel circuits
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own method and scope (Abstract, p.1).

papers.title_in_file: Dynamic parameterized quantum circuits: expressive and barren-plateau free
papers.what_it_is: A theory and numerics paper on parameterized circuits with mid-circuit measurement and feedforward.

assertions.value: The authors state that they prove absence of barren plateaus for local observables in dynamic parameterized circuits when the feedforward distance is constant.
quotes: we prove absence of barren plateaus for local observables under the condition that the feedforward distance f is constant
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1, Section I B 3, p.4 (informal statement of a proved result).

assertions.value: The authors state that adding ancilla qubits and feedforward operations to a unitary parameterized circuit gives a dynamic circuit at least as expressive as the original.
quotes: the resulting parameterized dynamic quantum circuit is at least as expressive as the original unitary parameterized quantum circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: Observation 1 argued directly in the text (Section I B 2).

assertions.value: The authors state that absence of barren plateaus does not imply trainability, and that whether worst-case hard instances for classical simulation arise during training is an open question.
quotes: absence of barren plateaus does not imply trainability, and it remains an open question whether worst-case hard instances for classical simulation can be encountered during the training of DPQC models
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own limit (Section VII, p.22).

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains an open task whether the good training behavior seen numerically persists for larger system sizes.
quotes: it remains an open task for future research to investigate whether the observed good training behavior persists for larger system sizes
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own limit (Section VII, p.22).

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Advantage: A Single Qubit's Experimental Edge in Classical Data Storage
papers.what_it_is: A photonic experiment showing a single qubit beating a classical bit in a communication game without shared randomness.

assertions.value: The authors report a quantum advantage in a scenario devoid of any shared randomness.
quotes: our results reveal a quantum advantage in a scenario devoid of any shared randomness
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one experiment.

assertions.value: The authors report a squared statistical overlap of 0.9998 ± 0.0016 averaged over the games, in agreement with theory.
quotes: squared statistical overlap of 0.9998 ± 0.0016 averaged over the games
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that conventional wisdom, supported by the no-go theorems of Holevo and Frenkel-Weiner, suggests such an advantage is unattainable when sender and receiver share randomness or classical correlations.
quotes: Conventional wisdom, supported by the no-go theorems of Holevo and Frenkel-Weiner, suggests that such a quantum advantage is unattainable when the sender and receiver share randomness or classical correlations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to earlier work.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural networks to improve molecular protein binding affinity predictions
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid quantum-classical 3D CNN for drug binding affinity, tested in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hybrid network reduces the complexity of the classical network by 20% while maintaining optimal prediction performance.
quotes: reduce by 20% the complexity of the classical network while maintaining optimal performance in the predictions
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report time savings of up to 40% in the training process.
quotes: time savings of up to 40% in the training process
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that if the error probability is smaller than 0.01, a commonly-used error mitigation technique can accurately recover the noiseless outputs.
quotes: if the error probability is smaller than 0.01, a commonly-used error mitigation technique can accurately recover the noiseless outputs
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulated noise models.

assertions.value: The authors state that the models are evaluated against the core set of the 2020 PDBBind dataset.
quotes: The performance of the models is evaluated against the core set of the 2020 PDBBind dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own evaluation setup (Section III).

papers.title_in_file: Introducing Quantum Computing to High-School Curricula: A Global Perspective
papers.what_it_is: A position paper on adding quantum computing topics to high-school STEM curricula.

assertions.value: The authors state that their analysis demonstrates integrating quantum topics at the secondary level is feasible and can enrich STEM learning.
quotes: Our analysis demonstrates that integrating quantum topics at the secondary level is feasible and can enrich STEM learning.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim; the paper is a discussion, not an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that they suggest a modular approach inside existing subjects rather than a standalone quantum computing course.
quotes: Rather than proposing a standalone quantum computing course, we suggest a modular approach
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope (Introduction, p.1).

assertions.value: The authors state that access to quantum education remains uneven, particularly for students in under-resourced regions.
quotes: access to quantum education remains uneven, particularly for students in under-resourced regions
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim.

papers.title_in_file: Detecting Errors in a Quantum Network with Pauli Checks
papers.what_it_is: An analytic and simulation paper applying Pauli check sandwiching to quantum networks.

assertions.value: The authors report that PCS outperforms BBPSSW rounds 1, 2 and 3 in fidelity for a comparable number of input qubits over most values of initial fidelity.
quotes: In terms of fidelity, it outperforms BBPSSW round 1, 2, and 3 for a comparable number of input qubits and over most of the values of the initial fidelity.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytic and simulated comparison from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that recursive PCS X&Z generates a family of distance 2 codes locally equivalent to CSS codes with a maximum stabilizer generator weight of 4.
quotes: Recursive PCS X&Z generates a family of distance 2 codes that are locally equivalent to CSS codes and have a maximum stabilizer generator weight of 4.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author-derived result.

assertions.value: The authors state that PCS protects the targeted qubits and generally needs less resource overhead than standard error correction and detection codes.
quotes: PCS provides protection on the targeted qubits and generally requires less resource overhead than standard quantum error correction and detection codes
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim supported by cited work.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Federated Learning: Analysis, Design and Implementation Challenges
papers.what_it_is: A survey and position paper on quantum federated learning.

assertions.value: The authors state that the focus of the work is to fill the gap of extremely limited QFL studies and their designs.
quotes: Our primary focus in this work is to fill the gap of extremely limited QFL studies and their designs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement; a survey with no experiments.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum data availability and analyses are still in their infancy.
quotes: quantum data availability and analyses are still in their infancy
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement.

assertions.value: The authors state that the current availability of quantum devices is limited to NISQ devices.
quotes: the current availability of quantum devices is limited to noisy mid-scale quantum (NISQ) devices
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement.
